_note: THE ONE FILE. Every colour, size, spacing, duration, layout constant and user-facing string in the product. Changing this restyles the whole box; nothing else should need touching. Loaded by launcher/theme.js, which stamps `tokens` onto :root as CSS custom properties and hands `motion`, `layout` and `copy` to JS. Keys become CSS vars by their path: tokens.color.ink -> --ink, tokens.size.bar -> --size-bar. Comments live in _note keys, the way server/config.json already does it.
name: NOTHING

color._note: Pure black, one ink, one red accent. The greys are a ladder, not a palette — dim for secondary text, faint for tertiary, rule for hairlines, panel for the only non-black surface. Adding a second accent is how this stops looking like a Nothing product.

font._note: Two roles. Display is the dot-matrix engine (drawn, not typed — constraint 8 forbids font CDNs), used for the clock, channel numbers and headings; it is Latin-only and that is fine because it only ever carries numbers and short uppercase words. Body carries content — Macedonian Cyrillic and Greek included — so it must have real coverage. The stack below resolves to system faces today; ship a woff2 here before this leaves the house.
font.body: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

size._note: clamp() triples as min/preferred/max. The box runs at one resolution, but dev happens in a window, so nothing is allowed to be a fixed pixel value.
size.title: clamp(16px, 2vw, 26px)

track._note: Letterspacing. Uppercase mono at these tracking values is the label voice of the whole UI.
track.label: 0.32em

space._note: A scale, not arbitrary values. Everything in the UI picks from this ladder.

line._note: Hairlines only. This UI has no borders thicker than a rule and no radii — a rounded card is the single fastest way to make it look like a streaming app.

glow._note: Selection is a white glow, not a coloured edge. A red bar under the selected poster read as a progress indicator and fought with the artwork; light coming off the card reads as focus and works over any poster. The red accent is spent on the one dot that marks state, nowhere else.

fade._note: Edge masks, as a percentage of the element's width. The news marquee fades out before it reaches its category label rather than sliding under it — 3% is enough to read as a fade and not as a cut.
fade._note-review: The vertical equivalent, for the review paragraph as it auto-scrolls: a fade at whichever end has text beyond it, so a half-line at the edge reads as 'there is more' instead of as a cut-off word. Bigger than the horizontal one because a line of body copy is taller than it is thin.

motion._note: Expressive but restrained: things assemble rather than slide, and nothing bounces. Durations are milliseconds. The `lite` profile cuts these; see profiles.
motion._note-review-scroll: A review longer than the panel scrolls itself rather than being clipped at the fourth line. Same idea as the news marquee and the same unit: px/s against the real overflow, so a long review and a slightly-too-long one crawl at one readable speed instead of one duration. review-scroll-hold is the pause at the top and again at the bottom, so the first and last lines can be read before anything moves.

layout._note: Structure, not style. Changing these re-proportions screens without touching their code.
layout._note-posters: A page is `grid-rows-per-page` rows deep; the viewport shows however many fit (two, at 1080p with six columns) and scrolls through the rest. Reaching the bottom of a page turns to the next one. This is a memory budget as much as a layout one — every card is a real image decode.
layout._note-detail-bottom: The bottom half of the detail panel has two occupants and never both: a film's reviews, or a show's season tabs and episode list. Both hang off the plot above them and the hints claim whatever is left, so raising either of these eats empty space rather than moving anything.
layout._note-channels: The channel list is a window onto the dial, not the whole of it: `channel-list-rows` rows are drawn and the slice moves with the cursor, so a hundred-channel m3u costs the same to draw as a ten-channel one.
layout._note-sources: The stream picker, same windowing rule as the channel list and for the same reason — a popular film comes back with sixty copies and only eight of them are ever on screen. `source-dot` sizes the dot-matrix quality tag that opens each row, which is the picker's equivalent of a channel number.

copy._note: Every user-facing string. Localisation lives here; nothing in the code hardcodes English.

detail._note-sources: The stream picker. Every copy of a title the addons know about, so a dead or badly-seeded source is one press away from a different one rather than a dead end. `direct` marks a debrid link, which plays immediately; everything else is a torrent that has to buffer. `outside` marks a stream past the playback envelope set in stremio.py.

tv._note: The channel list — the dial made visible. TV is the one screen where numbers still mean something, so this is the only place they are ever browsed.

profiles._note: Hardware profiles. The base values target the x86 boxes this now runs on — a Fedora laptop for development, an AMD-GPU machine in production. `lite` is a generic low-power fallback: less motion, fewer images in flight, a slower marquee. It was `pi3` until August 2026, when the Raspberry Pi 3B+ stopped being a target; the numbers are the ones that kept a 1 GB board usable, which makes them a sensible floor for any weak machine rather than a description of one. Selected by theme.js from ?profile= or the backend's config.
